help.intro: Saying where you are is something you do every day — Ich bin im Büro, wir sind in der Stadt, sie ist bei ihren Eltern — and a small set of prepositions covers it: in, an, auf, bei, aus, von, vor, unter (and nach for Wohin?, which has its own quiz in the next module). Behind them sits the dative case, which changes der to dem and die to der, and glues in + dem into im and an + dem into am. You will learn the dative as a system later in the course. For now you learn these as fixed chunks, the way a child does: im Park, am Bahnhof, in der Schule, bei Siemens, beim Arzt. The pairing is what matters: in for inside or in a town or country, an for at (a station, the sea, the university), bei for at a person’s or a company’s, auf / vor / unter for on, in front of and under something, and for ‘from’ the mirror image — aus for out of a place, von for from a person, a company or a point.
help.tips[0].title: im / in der / in — inside, or in a place
help.tips[0].text: in + der-/das-word → im (im Park, im Büro, im Kino); in + die-word → in der (in der Schule, in der Stadt); towns and most countries: in Berlin, in Deutschland.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I am at the office. Anna is at school.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We live in Germany, in Cologne.
help.tips[0].check.why: das Kino is a das-word, so in + dem melts into im: im Kino, like im Büro.
help.tips[1].title: am / bei / beim — at
help.tips[1].text: am for a point or place you are at but not inside: am Bahnhof, am Meer, an der Uni. bei for a person's home or a company: bei meinen Eltern, bei Siemens, beim Arzt (bei + dem).
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: He works at Siemens. She's at the doctor's.
help.tips[1].check.q: Heute Abend esse ich ____ meiner Oma.
help.tips[1].check.why: At a person's home is bei: bei meiner Oma, bei meinen Eltern.
help.tips[2].title: aus / vom / von — from
help.tips[2].text: aus = out of a place you were inside (aus dem Büro, aus der Schule, aus Italien); von = from a person, a company, or an activity (von meinen Eltern, von Siemens, vom Arzt, von der Arbeit).
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: I've just come from the supermarket.
help.tips[2].trap: the article after these prepositions is dative: dem, der, den. English 'in the' never changes; German 'in dem' becomes 'im'. Learn the chunk, not the rule, for now.
help.tips[2].check.why: From a person is von, not aus (you were never inside the dentist), and von + dem becomes vom.
help.tips[3].title: auf / vor / unter — on, in front of, under
help.tips[3].text: For where a thing is: auf dem Tisch (on the table), vor dem Haus (in front of the house), unter dem Tisch (under the table). The dem after them is the same dative chunk as in im and am.
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: The book is lying on the table.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: The car is in front of the house.
help.tips[3].check.q: The cat is sleeping under the bed: Die Katze schläft ____ dem Bett.
help.tips[3].check.why: unter = under, auf = on, vor = in front of — each followed by the same dem chunk.
help.tips[4].title: im–am–beim: the three contractions
help.tips[4].text: in dem → im, an dem → am, bei dem → beim, von dem → vom. Whenever you hear a preposition ending in -m, it has swallowed a dem.
help.tips[4].examples[0].en: in bed, at the window, at the baker's, from the station
help.tips[4].examples[1].en: I'm at the office. She's at the doctor's.
help.tips[4].check.q: Which words are hidden inside beim?
help.tips[4].check.why: A preposition ending in -m has swallowed a dem: bei dem → beim, like in dem → im.
help.remember[0]: im = inside a der/das place · in der = inside a die place · am = at · bei = at someone's.
help.remember[1]: Mirror pairs: in ↔ aus (inside ↔ out of), bei ↔ von (at someone's ↔ from someone).
help.context.en: Where are you? – I'm still at the office. And you? – I'm in town, at the station. I've just come from the doctor's. – And Lena? – She's at her parents' in Hamburg. She's coming back from Hamburg tomorrow.
help.mistakes[0].why: in + dem is always contracted to im in speech and normal writing.
help.mistakes[1].why: At a company or a person's place is bei, not in.
help.mistakes[2].why: Origin from a country or city is aus; von is for people and points.
help.hook: Im Büro, am Bahnhof, beim Arzt — learn where-you-are as ready-made chunks and you can say where you are all day.
sentences[0].english: Where are you? – I am in the park.
sentences[0].why: Being somewhere (wo?) takes in + dative: der Park → dem Park, and in dem shrinks to im.
sentences[1].english: Where is Anna? – She is at the station.
sentences[1].why: At a point like the station it is an + dative: an dem → am Bahnhof.
sentences[2].english: Where is Tom? – He is at the supermarket.
sentences[2].why: Inside a building: in + dative; der Supermarkt → dem, and in dem = im.
sentences[3].english: Where are the children? – They are at school.
sentences[3].why: die-words take der in the dative: in der Schule.
sentences[4].english: Where are you? – We are in town.
sentences[4].why: wo? means dative, and die Stadt becomes der Stadt: in der Stadt.
sentences[5].english: Where is Mum? – She is in the kitchen.
sentences[5].why: die Küche in the dative is der Küche: in der Küche.
sentences[6].english: Where is Lisa? – She is at the university.
sentences[6].why: Institutions like the Uni take an + dative: an der Uni.
sentences[7].english: Where are you? – I am still at the office.
sentences[7].why: das-words take dem in the dative, and in dem shrinks to im: im Büro.
sentences[8].english: Where are Anna and Tom? – They are at the cinema.
sentences[8].why: das Kino → dem Kino; in dem = im Kino.
sentences[9].english: Where is the child? – It is already in bed.
sentences[9].why: Lying in bed is a place (wo?): in + dative — im Bett.
sentences[10].english: Where do you live? – We live in Germany.
sentences[10].why: Country names without an article take plain in: in Deutschland.
sentences[11].english: Where do you work? – I work at the bank.
sentences[11].why: Working at an employer is bei + dative: bei der Bank.
sentences[12].english: Where is Lena? – She is at my parents’.
sentences[12].why: At a person's place it is bei + dative; plural dative adds -n: bei meinen Eltern.
sentences[13].english: Where is Mr Braun? – He is at the doctor’s.
sentences[13].why: At a person (the doctor's) it is bei + dative: bei dem → beim Arzt.
sentences[14].english: Where are you coming from? – I am coming from the park.
sentences[14].why: Coming from somewhere (woher?) is aus or von + dative: aus dem Park.
sentences[15].english: Where is Anna coming from? – She is coming from the station.
sentences[15].why: From a point you were at (am Bahnhof) you come vom — von dem — Bahnhof.
sentences[16].english: Where are you coming from? – We are coming from the supermarket.
sentences[16].why: Out of a building is aus + dative: aus dem Supermarkt.
sentences[17].english: Where are the children coming from? – They are coming from school.
sentences[17].why: woher? takes dative: die Schule → der Schule — aus der Schule.
sentences[18].english: Where is Lisa coming from? – She is coming from the university.
sentences[18].why: From the Uni (where you are an der Uni) you come von der Uni — dative die → der.
sentences[19].english: Where are you coming from? – I am coming from the office.
sentences[19].why: Out of the building: aus + dative — das Büro → dem, aus dem Büro.
sentences[20].english: Where is he from? – He is from Berlin.
sentences[20].why: Towns and countries without an article take plain aus: aus Berlin.
sentences[21].english: Where is the letter from? – It is from the bank.
sentences[21].why: A letter comes from a sender: von + dative — von der Bank.
sentences[22].english: Where is Mr Braun coming from? – He is coming from the doctor’s.
sentences[22].why: From a person's place it is von + dative: von dem → vom Arzt — the pair of beim Arzt.
sentences[23].english: Where is the parcel from? – It is from my parents.
sentences[23].why: A parcel from people: von + dative, and the plural dative adds -n — von meinen Eltern.
sentences[24].english: The book is lying on the table.
sentences[24].why: auf is 'on top of'; lying somewhere is a position (wo?), so dative follows: auf dem Tisch.
sentences[25].english: The dog is sleeping under the table.
sentences[25].why: unter is 'under'; the dog stays put, so dative: unter dem Tisch.
sentences[26].sentence: Das Auto steht ____ dem Haus. (in front of)
sentences[26].english: The car is standing in front of the house.
sentences[26].why: vor is 'in front of'; the car is parked (wo?), so dative: vor dem Haus.
sentences[27].english: Where is Mum coming from? – She is coming from the kitchen.
sentences[27].why: Out of a room: aus + dative — aus der Küche.
sentences[28].english: Where are you from? – We are from Germany.
sentences[28].why: Origin from a country without an article: plain aus — aus Deutschland.
sentences[29].english: The cat is sleeping under the bed.
sentences[29].why: unter = 'under'; sleeping is staying in place, so dative follows: unter dem Bett.
sentences[30].english: The phone is lying on the bed.
sentences[30].why: auf = 'on'; the phone just lies there (wo?), so dative: auf dem Bett.
